title: Interleaved staging bridge with transactional snapback
author: Lena Cho
description:
Motivation: We need a low-latency path for mid-stage promotions that can interleave small batches of live traffic with shadow runs while providing a deterministic, transactional rollback (snapback) that preserves session affinity and allows replay-based debugging. This PR adds a staging bridge component that sits between the routing layer and the promotion controller; it supports interleaved traffic lanes (canary + shadow), a transactional snapback engine that atomically reverts routed sessions to the previous variant, and a replay runway for deterministic request capture and replay for postmortem/regression bisects.

What this changes (single-string body): Implements a new service-level component under service/rollout called the staging bridge. The bridge exposes a minimal config surface (stagingPolicy v1) to the control plane and integrates with existing rollout orchestration: it subscribes to traffic tables and model version graphs, applies per-cohort lane weights, records request signatures for sessions that opt into replay capture, and provides an atomic "snapback" operation that rolls routed sessions back with guaranteed ordering. The snapback engine uses checkpointed routing state plus a short-lived shadow drain window to ensure no client is routed to a swapped variant mid-transaction. The bridge is resilient to partial failures by using lease-backed checkpointing and a small ringbuffer-backed WAL for in-flight session metadata.

Key files changed: controlplane/api/v1/rollout.proto (adds StagingPolicy message and SnapbackRequest), service/rollout/bridge.go (core bridge implementation), service/rollout/snapback_engine.go (transactional revert logic), service/rollout/bridge_test.go (unit tests), e2e/tests/staging_bridge_e2e.yaml (integration harness), console/src/components/rollout/stagingBridge.tsx (console UI to visualize lanes and trigger snapback), docs/runbooks/staging-bridge.md (operator runbook), docs/api/staging-policy.md (schema and examples).

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (Linear: ENG-3124) - [x] Wire up control plane protobuf & validation - [x] Unit tests for snapback ordering invariants - [x] Integration test reproducing interleaved routing + rollback - [x] Console visualization for manual operator inspection - [x] Runbook and migration notes included - [x] Load-tested in perf-canary (small cluster)

Operational notes: The staging bridge is opt-in per rollout via stagingPolicy on the rollout spec. Default behavior remains unchanged. New stagingPolicy fields: maximum interleave fraction, replay_ttl_seconds, snapback_grace_window_ms. Operators can trigger a snapback via the console button or the control-plane endpoint /v1/rollouts/{id}/snapback which accepts reason and target cohort. Snapback is implemented as a coordinated two-phase operation: 1) freeze new traffic assignments for cohorts in scope and checkpoint current routing map; 2) atomically flip routing bindings and open a shadow drain window to allow in-flight requests to finish. If snapback fails to reach quorum within the grace window it aborts and emits a detailed audit event for manual review.

Backward compatibility: The control plane rejects stagingPolicy v1 if the bridge feature flag is not enabled. Existing rollouts that do not reference stagingPolicy are unaffected. Migration guide in docs/runbooks/staging-bridge.md explains how to incrementally adopt the feature on Dedicated clusters; we recommend starting with replay_ttl_seconds=60 and max_interleave_fraction=0.05.

Testing and performance: Unit tests cover ordering, lease failure modes, and WAL recovery. E2E harness simulates 2000 concurrent sessions with mixed short/long-running requests; observed median increase in p50 routing latency is +3.2ms with 99th percentile remaining within SLO for the small perf-canary cluster used in tests. The staging bridge includes an adaptive fast-path that bypasses WAL for cohorts with low interleave fractions to reduce overhead.

Security and audit: Snapback actions are recorded in audit logs with reason, operator, and snapshot hash. Access to snapback API is gated by existing RBAC policies; we added a new permission scope rollout:snapback.

Related: ENG-3124 (design), ENG-3201 (e2e harness), SUP-1428 (customer incident that motivated deterministic revert), doc:docs/runbooks/staging-bridge.md.

Review conversation summary (concise, single string): Marco Nguyen: "Nice design, one concern: snapback lease acquisition may deadlock if the promotion controller also holds the epoch lock; can we use non-blocking try-acquire with fallback?" Author (Lena Cho): "Addressed: changed lease acquisition to try-acquire with an exponential backoff and explicit abort path; added unit tests to simulate the contention and ensured no deadlock in the harness." Ava Martinez: "UI looks good but we should surface the snapshot hash and truncated sample of captured request signatures for operators." Author: "Added snapshot hash and a capped sample (up to 10 entries) to the console card; sample is redacted to avoid PII leakage." Ravi Kapoor: "Small nit on proto naming; SnapbackRequest should include an optional operator_id field for audit traces." Author: "Added operator_id and updated docs; validated backward compatibility in proto migration tests." Marco Nguyen: "Verified; approving." Ava Martinez: "Approving after docs update." CI: initial run had flaky failure in e2e (timeout on perf-canary); rerun passed; final status: all checks green.

Merge: squash and merge after approvals, merged by Marco Nguyen on 2025-11-20. Post-merge steps: feature flag rollout (gradual), create release note blurb, coordinate with SRE for Dedicated rollout window.
